summary: Background I/O polling daemon causes fractional GPU starvation and intermittent stream stalls in dedicated pool
description:
Issue summary: Customer LumenHealth reported periodic stream stalls and throughput collapse in their dedicated GPU pool. Impact: A subset of short streaming requests for low-latency chat UIs experienced p50->p99 regressions and intermittent 502/stream disconnects for ~2 hours during peak. Environment: prod-us-west, dedicated pool ID ded-42, tenant 'lumen-health', mixed short/long streams.

Observed behavior: P99 latency spikes correlated with short stream fanout and sustained elevated GPU PCIe/host IO wait. Metrics show fractional GPU utilization dips and transient NVMe write bursts from background sidecar daemon (checkpointing/log-forwarding) that coincided with GPU batchers stalling. Autoscaler did not immediately react due to smoothing window.

Business impact: Customer-facing chat UI saw degraded experience; LumenHealth support flagged at P1 and requested immediate mitigation and RCA.

Attachments: timeline graph slices, top-of-host iostat samples, serving runtime debug logs (snippets below).
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Provision a dedicated pool (ded-42) with mixed short-stream and medium-batch traffic.
2) Deploy tenant 'lumen-health' with streaming endpoints pinned to redwood-1.1-small.
3) Run sustained short streaming fanout load (many concurrent ~300ms streams) while a background sidecar job performs frequent checkpointing and log flushes to local NVMe.
4) Observe p99 latency and GPU queueing on serving-runtime dashboards; iostat shows bursts.
logs: 2026-02-26T14:03:15Z kernel: nvme0n1: write queue depth surge -> host_busy (io_wait)
investigation_notes: Initial triage (Riley): Dashboard correlation between p99 spikes and host nvme write bursts. P50 remained stable, indicating small subset of batches blocked waiting on host IO.
Support->SRE (Anika Patel): Confirmed sidecar jobs on hosts were running checkpointing every ~30-60s. Observed kernel-level io wait and occasional PCIe bandwidth saturation.

Hypothesis (Marcus): Background I/O from sidecar caused periodic host IO saturation which increased host-side latency for GPU batchers, creating fractional GPU starvation and stream stalls. Autoscaler smoothing delayed reactive scale-up.
Test (SRE): Disabled sidecar checkpoint flushes on one host and reproducer load; p99 returned to baseline within 2 minutes. Re-enabled to confirm regression.
Related: linked to SUP-742998 where pcie saturation was implicated in p99 drops but that ticket focused on tenant IO; this ticket isolated sidecar daemon as root cause.
comments: Riley Chen (Support) 2026-02-26: Noted customer saw first occurrence during Tuesday morning peak; uploaded dashboards to ticket and pinged #support.
Anika Patel (SRE) 2026-02-26: Running host-level audit; found sidecar checkpoint jobs scheduled by default cron (frequency 60s). Will test increasing interval.
Marcus O'Neill (Infra Eng) 2026-02-26: Can we push a config change to reduce flush frequency and add token-bucket rate-limiter on sidecar writes for affected pool? Prepared PR #4823.
LumenHealth (Customer) 2026-02-26: Thank you — we are seeing intermittent disconnects. Please advise ETA for mitigation.
Marcus O'Neill (Infra Eng) 2026-02-27: Hotfix pushed to sidecar config (checkpoint interval 10m + write rate cap 10MB/s). Monitoring closely.
Riley Chen (Support) 2026-03-02: Customer confirmed improvement; no further stream disconnects reported in the follow-up window.
root_cause_analysis: Background sidecar checkpointing and log flushes on dedicated pool hosts were scheduled too aggressively (default 30–60s). When combined with a high-concurrency short-stream workload, the resulting NVMe write bursts caused host IO wait spikes and transient GPU batcher stalls. Autoscaler smoothing prevented immediate scale-up, prolonging impact. Net effect: fractional GPU starvation for affected tenants leading to p99 latency spikes and occasional stream disconnects.
resolution_notes: 1) Immediate mitigation: Deployed hotfix to sidecar configuration for ded-42 to increase checkpoint interval to 10 minutes and apply token-bucket rate limiting on writes. This removed the NVMe burst pattern and p99 returned to baseline.
2) Autoscaler tuning: Reduced smoothing_window from 120s to 30s for short-stream-heavy tenant profiles and added a fast-path trigger based on host_io_wait metric.
3) Longer-term: Added an integration test in runtime CI to simulate background I/O during short-stream fanout and catch regressions. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4823
4) Customer follow-up: Notified LumenHealth that fix deployed and asked to validate; scheduled a 1-week monitoring check-in.
5) Postmortem: Created Confluence runbook updates with guidance for sidecar flush defaults and a gating checklist before dedicated pool onboarding.
resolution: Hotfix deployed to sidecar configs + autoscaler parameter adjustment; monitoring shows stable p99 and customer validated satisfaction. Ticket closed after 7-day observation window.
